|affiliation=[[Galactic Empire]] }} The '''TIE/rb heavy starfighter''', more formally known as the '''TIE reinforcement battery heavy starfighter''', and simply known as the '''heavy TIE fighter''', '''TIE Brute''', or the '''Infiltrator''' was a variant of the [[TIE series|TIE fighter series]] [[starfighter]]s used by the [[Galactic Empire]], distinguished by its extra pod housing more powerful [[laser cannon]]s. ==Characteristics== [[File:TIEbrute-WIRED.png|thumb|left|250px|Forward view of a TIE Brute]] The TIE/rb heavy [[starfighter]] was an [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] craft of the [[TIE series|TIE fighter series]]. Unlike the regular [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter|TIE/LN starfighter]], it was equipped with life support and a pressure controlled cockpit. As the fighter was theorized to be a larger target, the [[viewport]] was made of extra-reinforced [[transparisteel]]. The TIE/rb also was a bulked-up version of the TIE/In with heavier armor and a secondary pod which housed a [[MGK-300 integrated droid brain]] that assisted with inflight support, in a manner similar to an [[astromech droid]]. The pod also housed twin [[H-s9.3 twin laser cannon]]s. ==History== The prototype was created by [[Sienar Fleet Systems]] in response to the Empire's expansion into the [[Outer Rim Territories]]. A [[Unidentified Sienar designer|designer]] at SFS led a team in trying to arm the standard TIE model with the heavier H-s9.3 cannons, which it could not handle. The weapons were then placed in an outrigger pod, becoming the basis for the TIE Brute.''[[Starships and Speeders]]'' Some Imperial [[admiral]]s were wary of its development, believing it would reduce the need for larger support vessels. Like all TIE models, they were manufactured by Sienar Fleet Systems, and featured [[twin ion engine]]s and micro-corrugated [[solar collector]] panels,''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]'' with the power being transferred via a conduit located between the panel and the engine systems. The pilot was assisted by a [[droid]] intelligence system, which acted in a similar manner to an [[Astromech droid|astromech]] counterpart. At least three of the starfighters were assigned to the [[Kullgroon]] [[garrison]]. They were deployed during the [[Job on Kullgroon|uprising]] on the planet led by [[Captain]] [[Landonis Balthazar Calrissian|Lando Calrissian]] and the natives. They were all shot down by [[L3-37]] flying the [[YT-1300 light freighter|starship]] ''[[Millennium Falcon]]''.[[Lando - Double or Nothing 5|''Lando - Double or Nothing'' 5]]
[[File:TIEBrute-SaS.png|thumb|left|220px|TIE Brutes launch with standard TIEs from the Carida Academy.]]
[[Cadet]] [[Han Solo]], during his time at the [[Carida Academy]], was assigned to fly a TIE Brute aboard a''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story: Expanded Edition]]'' [[Cantwell-class Arrestor Cruiser|''Cantwell''-class Arrestor Cruiser]]''[[Starships and Speeders]]'' as part of [[Onyx Squadron]]. His ship was damaged during a fight with pirates and crashed in the landing bay, leading to a [[Tribunal of Han Solo|tribunal]]. In [[10 BBY]], one such fighter was again deployed to chase the ''Millennium Falcon'' inside the [[Akkadese Maelstrom]] and was the last surviving TIE fighter pursuing the ''Falcon'' until Solo, now an outlaw, used a maneuver he learned from a [[Needles|street racer]] on [[Corellia]], causing the TIE/rb to crash. Following the [[Galactic Civil War]], the Imperial successor state known as the [[First Order]] used a [[First Order TIE/rb heavy starfighter|similar model of fighter]] during their own [[First Order-Resistance War|war]] with the [[Resistance]]. {{Ship-stub}} ==Behind the scenes== The TIE/rb was first revealed in the very first look at the ''[[Star Wars Anthology Series]]'' film ''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]'', the "Big Game" TV spot released during [[Wikipedia:Super Bowl LII|Super Bowl LII]].{{SWYouTube|9Szts88zY4o|Solo: A Star Wars Story "Big Game" TV Spot (:45)|sw_url=video/big-game-tv-spot-solo-a-star-wars-story}} Its design, done by [[James Clyne]], was originally proposed for [[Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens|''Star Wars'': Episode VII ''The Force Awakens'']]. It was added to ''Solo'' when the crew decided they needed a "leader" TIE fighter. One of its nicknames was the "Bubba" TIE.''[[The Art of Solo: A Star Wars Story]]'' ==Appearances== *''[[Star Wars: Starfighter Missions]]'' *[[Han Solo - Imperial Cadet 1|''Han Solo - Imperial
